CAN_ASSUME_WEB_IDENTITY.description: AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity admitted by the trust policy; props.admits = any | pattern | specific.

CAN_ESCALATE.description: Self-escalation, or modification of a principal the source can already act as (closure, engine.md §4.6); evidence.chain lists the edge ids.

CAN_MODIFY_PERMISSIONS_OF.description: Put*/Attach*Policy, CreatePolicyVersion, SetDefaultPolicyVersion or boundary changes on another principal. Closure input: becomes CAN_ESCALATE when the target is reachable.

CAN_REACH_NODE_IMDS.description: The pod can reach the node's IMDS (hop limit, hostNetwork); Fargate excluded. evidence.weight_extra adds 0-2 by hop limit.

CAN_RUN_AS_SA.description: The role can create pods or tokens in the service account's namespace.

CAN_TAKEOVER.description: Credential or trust takeover of another principal: CreateAccessKey, Create/UpdateLoginProfile, UpdateAssumeRolePolicy, AddUserToGroup. Self is excluded.

CLUSTER_ROLE.description: EKS control-plane service role; workloads never get it.

FULL_ACCESS.description: s3:* (identity policy or same-account bucket-policy grant).

HAS_POLICY.description: Managed policy attached to the principal (ARN-keyed).

INGRESS_ROUTES_TO.description: Ingress rule routes to the service. Renamed from the K8s EXPOSES.

IRSA_BRIDGE.description: IRSA: the annotated role trusts this service account through the cluster's OIDC provider.

IS_ADMIN_EQUIVALENT.description: The principal is admin-equivalent (ADMIN-001), so reaching it means reaching the account admin.

NODE_ROLE.description: Node instance role, reachable through node IMDS.

PUBLIC_INBOUND.description: Reachable from the internet (security groups, routes, NACLs, scheme, endpoint access). INTERNET_FACING is folded into props.igw_routed.

RUNS_AS.description: The pod mounts the service-account token (automount on).

SELECTS.description: Service selector routes to the pod.

SERVICE_CAN_ASSUME.description: The trust policy admits an AWS service principal (PassRole candidates, confused-deputy checks).

evaluation_gaps.detail: The report predates _coverage.json: denied or failed collection cannot be told apart from empty data.
Identity policies of external principals are not visible; cross-account edges are conditional.
IAM was collected with the per-entity (d13c215) layout: no policy versions, no identity providers, boundaries and tags may be missing
Resource control policies are unknown (membership unknown)
Service control policies are unknown (membership unknown)
Condition values known only at request time (source IP, MFA, tags in the request) are not evaluated; such decisions are conditional.
Session policies passed at AssumeRole time can only narrow permissions and are not modelled.

findings.description: This role is administrator-equivalent: its effective permissions allow every action on every resource. Its 64 individual privilege-escalation and dangerous-permission findings are summarised here.
findings.remediation: Treat this principal as an account administrator: limit who can use it (trust policy, group membership, credentials), require MFA, and replace broad grants (Action:* or iam:*) by the permissions it needs.
findings.title: Administrator-equivalent principal

findings.description: Every pod running as service account payments/payments-sa can assume arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/demo-irsa-admin, which is administrator-equivalent in AWS: compromising one such pod compromises the account.
findings.remediation: Restrict the role to the permissions the workload needs, and scope its trust policy to this service account (exact sub and aud conditions).
findings.title: Service account can assume an admin IAM role through IRSA (payments/payments-sa, cluster demo-eks)

findings.description: ClusterRoleBinding 'ci-deployer-admin' grants kube-system/ci-deployer every verb on every resource in the whole cluster. Every pod running as this service account controls the cluster.
findings.remediation: Use a more restrictive ClusterRole or a namespaced Role.
findings.title: ServiceAccount kube-system/ci-deployer bound to cluster-admin (cluster demo-eks)

findings.description: The pod shares the host's network namespace (every node interface, the node's IMDS).
findings.title: Pod uses hostNetwork (kube-system/node-debugger, cluster demo-eks)

findings.description: The pod shares the host's PID namespace (it can see and signal every process on the node).
findings.title: Pod uses hostPID (kube-system/node-debugger, cluster demo-eks)

findings.description: Service web/web-lb of type LoadBalancer gets an internet-facing AWS load balancer (in-tree cloud provider default (internet-facing)), open to any source address.
findings.remediation: Use an internal load balancer (service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-scheme: internal) or restrict loadBalancerSourceRanges.
findings.title: Service web/web-lb is an internet-facing load balancer (cluster demo-eks)

findings.description: A privileged container (regular, init or ephemeral) has every capability and the host's devices: it can take over the node.
findings.remediation: Remove privileged: true (regular, init and ephemeral containers).
findings.title: Privileged container (kube-system/node-debugger, cluster demo-eks)

findings.description: ClusterRole 'demo-wildcard' allows every verb on every resource; whoever is bound to it has unrestricted access to the cluster.
findings.remediation: Restrict verbs and resources to least privilege.
findings.title: ClusterRole demo-wildcard allows * on * (cluster demo-eks)

findings.description: The Kubernetes API endpoint of cluster demo-eks (eu-west-2) is publicly accessible from 0.0.0.0/0. Authentication is still required, but any leaked kubeconfig, token or mapped IAM credential is usable from anywhere, and API-server vulnerabilities are exposed.
findings.remediation: Disable public endpoint access, or restrict publicAccessCidrs to known administration networks.
findings.title: EKS cluster demo-eks has a public API endpoint open to the internet

findings.remediation: Require the provider's audience (<host>:aud) and an exact subject (<host>:sub), e.g. repo:<org>/<repo>:ref:refs/heads/main for GitHub or system:serviceaccount:<ns>:<sa> for EKS.
findings.title: Role 'demo-irsa-reader' trusts eks identities (pattern subjects)

findings.description: The IAM password policy is below common baselines: password reuse prevention None < 24.
findings.remediation: Set an account password policy: length >= 14, all character classes, reuse prevention 24.
findings.title: The account password policy is weak

findings.description: The pods mount the API token of their namespace's default service account. Use a dedicated service account, or set automountServiceAccountToken: false.
findings.remediation: Create a dedicated ServiceAccount for this workload, or set automountServiceAccountToken: false.
findings.title: Workload runs as the default service account with its token mounted (default/legacy-app, cluster demo-eks)

findings.description: The pods mount the API token of their namespace's default service account. Use a dedicated service account, or set automountServiceAccountToken: false.
findings.remediation: Create a dedicated ServiceAccount for this workload, or set automountServiceAccountToken: false.
findings.title: Workload runs as the default service account with its token mounted (kube-system/node-debugger, cluster demo-eks)

findings.remediation: Require the provider's audience (<host>:aud) and an exact subject (<host>:sub), e.g. repo:<org>/<repo>:ref:refs/heads/main for GitHub or system:serviceaccount:<ns>:<sa> for EKS.
findings.title: Role 'demo-irsa-admin' trusts eks identities (specific subjects)
